class: A question's choices drawn as pressable buttons were not read as its choices
symptom: Writer (Ashby), six runs on 28 September: 'Are you at least 18 years of age?', 'Are you legally authorized to work...?', 'Will you ... require employment visa sponsorship?' and the office-days question were handed over blank every time, though the profile answers all four.
site: Ashby job boards (any site that draws Yes/No as a row of aria-pressed buttons)
root_cause: The snapshot reader knew choices only as radios, checkboxes and dropdown options. Ashby's two <button aria-pressed> elements were read as ordinary buttons named 'Yes' and 'No', whose question was their own name, so nothing tied them to the question above and the profile pass never saw a question to answer. The older site adapter (sites/ashby.py answer_toggle) knew the row, but the reading agent that now fills forms does not use adapters for answers. Separately, the radio click path retried a click that raised, which on a toggle clears the answer it just gave.
why_tests_missed: Every choice fixture in the tests was a radio, checkbox or listbox; none drew a question's choices as buttons, and the one Ashby note lived only in a docstring of an adapter the reading agent no longer calls.
fix: parse_snapshot reads a row of two or more sibling buttons under a question (asked with '?', or with a pressed button, or named only Yes/No-style words) as that question's choices: role radio, group the question, checked when pressed, toggle=True. Action rows (Next, Back, Cancel, Edit, Remove, Attach...) are excluded. do() presses a toggle once through _press_toggle, leaves a pressed one alone, never falls back to another question's radios, and reads the page back: a press that did not stay is reported open.
prevention: Define 'a choice' by what a person sees -- several labelled things under one question, one of which is chosen -- not by the HTML role a site happens to use; build fixtures for each drawing of a choice (radio, checkbox, listbox, toggle button, card) from the start. When a site adapter learns a widget, the generic reader must learn it too, or the lesson is lost when the architecture moves on.
